counterfactual_missing_items: Coronary Artery CTA: No obvious abnormality
Normal sinus rhythm without ST-segment changes
decisive_items: myocardial edema in signal-enhanced T2-weighted imaging
One week after his 5th cycle of chemotherapy and immunotherapy
response.rationale: R3 is the most specific and complete diagnosis: CMR shows myocardial edema, elevated T2/T1, and LGE, with markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers shortly after immunotherapy, all supporting myocarditis. R5 is a broader cardiomyopathy label that captures myocardial injury/dysfunction but lacks the inflammatory and immunotherapy-linked specificity. R2 is only temporally linked, R4 is weakly supported by a small effusion with absent pericardial friction, and C1 is a redundant append-only variant of R5.

rejected.why: Append-only completion of R5 with only 'poor diastolic function'; redundant and lacks independent diagnostic specificity.
Only small pericardial effusion; no pericardial friction and CMR shows myocardial edema, not pericardial inflammation.
Raw support is only temporal relation to chemotherapy/immunotherapy; no raw cardiac span directly links it to the observed myocardial injury.
